newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy June bank loans rise but deposits fall -ABI.
newsitem.headline: Italy June bank loans rise but deposits fall -ABI.

text.p: Total loans in the Italian banking system rose in June but deposits slipped, the Italian Banking Association (ABI) said in its latest report.
Total loans by banks holding short-term deposits, accounting for all high street banks, rose 5.25 percent year on year in June to 912.0 trillion lire after a 4.41 percent rise in May.
Lira loans increased by 5.15 percent year on year to 830.0 trillion lire while foreign currency loans rose 8.29 percent to 82.0 trillion lire.
ABI said total deposits slipped 1.46 percent year on year in June to 863.0 trillion lire, although it noted that within this total, bond fund inflows jumped 70.89 percent to 214.5 trillion lire.
Referring to the first quarter of 1997, the report noted "a strongly divergent trend between bank deposits (savings and current accounts and certificates of deposit) and borrowing."
On bad loans, latest data for March showed that banks registered a fall in net bad loans against February, although gross bad loans increased.
Net bad loans, based on recovery value, declined to 65.67 trillion lire in March from 66.89 trillion in February, but posted a 2.3 percent rise over March last year.
ABI said gross bad loans increased to 116.22 trillion lire in March from 115.44 trillion in February, with a rise of 11.9 percent over March 1996.
The report said the falling trend in gross bad loans seen since the second half of 1996 and linked to an improvement in companies' economic and financial situation "seems to have been interrupted."
